👥 Facebook, X & Telegram · Lesson 3 of 4

Telegram Channels: No Algorithm, New Ways to Earn

6 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

Telegram has no feed algorithm deciding who sees your channel posts. Every post goes straight to subscribers. So your real enemy isn't the algorithm — it's the mute button.

That changes the game. On TikTok you fight for discovery. On Telegram you fight for attention you already have. Post too often, post filler, and people mute you — they still count as subscribers, but they stop seeing anything.

The one number that matters: views per post

Divide the average views on your last 10 posts by your subscriber count. That's your view rate. Ad buyers in the Telegram market commonly look for roughly 20–40% — treat that as a rough industry rule of thumb, not an official figure. A 3,000-member channel with 1,200 views per post is worth more to a sponsor than a 10,000-member channel with 900.

Three ways Telegram itself now pays channel owners

ToolHow it worksWho can use it
Ad revenue shareTelegram shows ads in your channel and gives you 50% of the revenue, paid in Toncoin (TON)Public channels with 1,000+ subscribers (since March 2024)
Paid postsYou post content subscribers unlock with Telegram StarsAny channel admin (not 18+ channels)
Suggested / paid posts from othersSomeone pays you Stars or TON to publish their post; you approve, edit or reprice itRolled out July 2025, initially for Premium users
💡 What most creators miss

The money is real but it is crypto-based. Stars can only be withdrawn 21 days after you receive them, through Fragment, converted to TON. Turning TON into shillings means using a crypto exchange or P2P trader — prices move daily and you carry that risk. Keep records: it's still income in KRA's eyes.

Telegram doesn't publish ad rates by country, so a Kenyan channel's ad revenue depends on how many ads Telegram sells against your audience. Treat it as a bonus until your own Monetization tab (Statistics → Monetization) shows real numbers.

Telegram's best job is the closer. It rarely helps strangers find you. It shines as the place your TikTok or Instagram followers go for something extra: job alerts, betting-free sports analysis, deals from an Eastleigh wholesaler, revision notes for KCSE. Discovery happens elsewhere; loyalty happens here.

What you won't get: spam. Max [2] posts a day.

⚡ Quick check

A sponsor is choosing between two Telegram channels. What should matter most?

Telegram delivers every post to subscribers, but muted or inactive members never see it. Average views per post is the real audience a sponsor is paying to reach.

🚀 EndaViral growth

First impressions for a new channel

A brand-new channel with 12 members looks like an empty room. A starting base of members can make a visitor more willing to join content you're proud of. It won't create views or Telegram ad revenue by itself — your posts do that.

See Telegram member packages →

Works best as social proof on content you're proud of. Bought numbers don't count toward monetisation, so keep them out of brand pitches.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. No feed algorithm: your threat is mutes, so post less and better.
  2. View rate (views ÷ subscribers) is your real size.
  3. Telegram pays via 50% ad share (1,000+ subs), paid posts and suggested posts — in TON and Stars.
  4. Stars withdraw after 21 days via Fragment; converting to KES carries crypto price risk.
